question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(0.8),$ calculate $P(2<X\le 6).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(0.8).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0.8{e}^{-0.8x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(2<X\le 6)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X\le 6) & ={\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}0.8{e}^{-0.8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-0.8x}{|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =-{e}^{-4.8}+{e}^{-1.6} \\  & ≈0.1937\end{aligned}
$$
